title: arXiv mathematics — daily notable papers, 10 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from concrete result claims and corroborating artifacts, not measured popularity; citation evidence is limited for papers announced today.

sections.title: A proof of the Erdős-Herzog-Piranian lemniscate conjecture
sections.abstract: For every monic complex polynomial of degree at least one, the author claims the unit lemniscate has length no greater than that of z^n−1, with equality exactly for its translated and rotated forms.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the Erdős–Herzog–Piranian length inequality for every monic polynomial and the stated equality characterization (arXiv abstract and HTML Theorem 1.3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Monic complex polynomials of degree n ≥ 1; compare the arclength of {z: |p(z)|=1} against the lemniscate for z^n−1.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof supplements analytic arguments with rigorous computer-assisted estimates over a finite degree range; the certificates and their implementation merit specialist review. The preprint is not presented here as peer-reviewed.

sections.title: Chvátal's Toughness Conjecture for Dense Almost Regular Graphs
sections.abstract: For each fixed α>0, the author claims every sufficiently large 4-tough graph with minimum degree at least αn and maximum-minus-minimum degree at most εn is Hamiltonian, and constructs 3/2-tough regular non-Hamiltonian examples of linear degree.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the 4-tough Hamiltonicity result with the stated degree hypotheses and constructs 3/2-tough regular non-Hamiltonian graphs (arXiv abstract and HTML Theorem 1.3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For every fixed α>0, there are ε>0 and n₀ such that the result holds for n≥n₀, minimum degree δ(G)≥αn, and degree spread Δ(G)−δ(G)≤εn.
sections.unique_caveat: This settles only a dense almost-regular regime, not Chvátal's unrestricted conjecture; the 4-tough theorem and 3/2-tough counterexamples leave a gap in the threshold.

sections.title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
sections.abstract: The author claims a complete classification of modular rank-two Nahm sums with rational symmetric positive-definite matrices and rational shifts, consisting of explicit families, split rank-one products, and 34 exceptional triples.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims that no further modular data occur in the specified rank-two rational setting, and that all distinguished Nahm points have joint degree at most four (arXiv abstract and HTML Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A rational symmetric positive-definite 2×2 matrix, rational shifts, and modular Nahm sums; classification is up to coordinate exchange and includes rational-point families, split products, and exceptional data.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification does not cover higher rank, nonsymmetric matrices, or irrational parameters. Its exhaustive arithmetic and computational certificates should be checked independently; the preprint is not presented as peer-reviewed.

sections.title: Average distance and maximum induced linear forest
sections.abstract: For every finite connected graph, the authors claim the 2009 conjectured upper bound that average pairwise distance is at most half the order of a largest induced linear forest.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove μ(G) ≤ L(G)/2, equivalently 4W(G) ≤ L(G)n(n−1), for every connected graph (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite connected graph G of order n; μ(G) is average distance, W(G) the Wiener index, and L(G) the maximum order of an induced subgraph whose components are paths.
sections.unique_caveat: The claim concerns this one global inequality; the abstract does not claim an equality classification or a stability theorem.

sections.title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
sections.abstract: The authors compare relative trace formulas for the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture, match regular orbits, formulate the associated fundamental lemma and smooth-transfer conjecture, and prove the fundamental lemma for the unit Hecke-algebra element.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra for the orthogonal Gan–Gross–Prasad model (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the orthogonal Gan–Gross–Prasad model and a comparison of relative trace formulas; the stated theorem is for the unit Hecke-algebra element.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract only claims the unit-element fundamental lemma; it formulates, rather than claims to prove, the smooth-transfer conjecture.

sections.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
sections.abstract: For three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes on the cubic torus, the authors claim a unique global strong solution for arbitrary mean-zero divergence-free H² initial data and independent steady H² forcing when a fixed odd-viscosity coefficient exceeds a norm-uniform sufficient threshold.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim global strong well-posedness above a sufficient odd-viscosity threshold, positive-time smoothness in the unforced case, and additional regularity regions for explicit bounded data and forcing (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional incompressible flow on the cubic torus with vertical-derivative-of-curl odd viscosity; initial data and steady force are real, mean-zero/divergence-free as appropriate, and in second-order Sobolev spaces.
sections.unique_caveat: The threshold is sufficient, not claimed sharp; the authors explicitly leave the sharp threshold for the original equation open, and the theorem depends on the added odd-viscosity term.
